ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is “Table 1,” comparing the population aging trends of country A and country B in 2000, 2010, and 2020; the columns include year, indicator, country A, and country B. The data for “proportion of elderly population” in the table show: in 2000, country A was 6.9%, country B was 16.2%; in 2010, country A was 8.5%, country B was 17.0%; in 2020, country A was 11.9%, country B was 20.8%. Then reason: To judge the timing of population aging, one can look at whether the “proportion of elderly population” reaches or exceeds the 7% aging judgment line. Country A was 8.5% by 2010, only then exceeding 7%, indicating that country A entered aging later than country B. Therefore, country B experienced population aging earlier.
